newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq accuses U.S., Britain of holding up oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Iraq accuses U.S., Britain of holding up oil deal.

text.p: An Iraqi official accused the United States and Britain on Tuesday of blocking implementation of an oil-for-food agreement with the United Nations.
"Six months of the deal had ended and six months more were added, but the United States and Britain are obstructing implementation of the deal," Baghdad mayor Nori Faisel al-Shahir told reporters.

Shahir said Iraq received less than half the goods supposed to reach the country during the first six months of the pact. From December to June Baghdad was permitted to sell $2 billion worth of oil to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian necessities for Iraqis affected by U.N. sanctions imposed for Baghdad's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The U.N. Security Council extended the pact for another six months from the beginning of June.

The mayor said that Baghdad municipality, which runs drinking water and waste systems in the capital, had not received anything from the $8.4 million allocated by the deal for sanitation and potable water schemes.

He said only three out of 11 items related to these systems that Iraq had agreed to import went through. The rest were rejected by the U.S. and British representatives at the U.N. sanctions committee on Iraq, he added.
Iraqi newspapers said ministers of oil, health and industry briefed Iraqi MPs on Monday on the oil pact and how the United States was putting obstacles in the path of implementing the agreement.
